summary: 1932 Aermotor MC-24 steel tower in the Gila National Forest, Grant County; cab replaced 1966; NHLR-registered 2022; reached by the Signal Peak Trail from NM 15.

facts.design: 30-foot Aermotor MC-24 steel tower; the original cab was replaced in 1966 with a cab built to a Forest Service standard plan in the CL-100 to CL-106 series
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Gila National Forest

access.note: Reached by a Forest Service trail with trailhead parking; the sources do not say whether the tower itself is open to climbing.

visit.trail_note: Signal Peak Trail from the trailhead on NM 15, about 16.5 miles north of Silver City

events.note: Aermotor MC-24 steel tower erected in 1932

notes_for_editor: The NHLR page gives the build and cab history; the Forest Service trail page gives the access details. Do not confuse this with the Arizona Signal Peak Lookout on the Tonto National Forest, which search results also returned. An FFLA Facebook post titled 'First report! The Signal Peak...' reportedly mentions a call-in during the Skate fire, but the page would not load beyond its title, so no fire claim is made; this is a lead for the editor. Staffing and fire history were not found. height_m 9.1 converts the register's 30-foot height and may not equal the cab-floor height. Not verified: current condition, and whether the tower is closed to climbing.
